Section 5.1 — Confidentiality and Its Limits

A pastor is, among other things, a keeper of confidences. People will tell him things they have told no one else on earth — old sins, present fears, the secret griefs of a marriage, the failures they would die before letting the congregation see. This trust is one of the most sacred things entrusted to the office, and it is built slowly and shattered instantly. A man known to repeat what he hears in private will soon find that no one tells him anything that matters, and a pastor whom no one trusts with the truth cannot shepherd anyone's soul. Guard the confidences of your people as you would guard your own honor, for in handling them you are handling their honor.

And yet — and this is the part the textbooks too often pass over — confidentiality is a stewardship, not an absolute. It serves the good of the soul and the protection of the flock; it was never meant to become a wall behind which evil hides and the vulnerable are sacrificed. There are confidences a faithful pastor must not keep, and a man who does not settle this in advance will be paralyzed in the very moment he most needs clarity. The governing principle is this: the seal of confidence yields when keeping it would leave someone in danger of serious harm.

Consider the plainest cases. When a person discloses that he intends to take his own life or to harm another, the pastor's duty to protect life overrides his promise of secrecy; he must act to get that person real and immediate help, not merely pray and say nothing. When a child or other vulnerable person is being abused, the pastor is not free to bury that disclosure in the name of confidentiality; the protection of the helpless and, very often, the requirements of the law oblige him to bring it into the light and to involve the authorities and protective help that God has appointed for exactly such evils. To stay silent in these cases is not discretion; it is complicity. The shepherd who shields a wolf to keep a confidence has betrayed the sheep he was set to guard. Know the reporting laws of your own land, settle your conscience before the crisis comes, and resolve that you will never let a misplaced loyalty to secrecy make you an accomplice to harm.

Hold these two truths together, then, without letting go of either. Be a man whose mouth can be trusted with a thousand ordinary secrets — and be a man who knows the few, grave moments when love for the endangered must break the seal.
Section 5.2 — Power, Proximity, and Sexual Boundaries

We must speak frankly about something the pastor is often slow to admit: he holds real power. He is trusted, respected, granted spiritual authority, and given intimate access to people at their most vulnerable — the grieving, the lonely, the broken, the spiritually hungry. That combination of power and proximity is precisely the soil in which the gravest pastoral failures grow. And here is a truth that must be stated without flinching: because of that imbalance of power, a sexual or romantic entanglement between a pastor and someone under his spiritual care is never a meeting of equals, and the language of "it was mutual" is a lie the guilty tell themselves. The shepherd who preys on a sheep he was meant to feed has not had an affair; he has committed an abuse of the trust of his office, and the greater share of the guilt is his because the greater share of the power was his.

Because the danger is so real and so destructive, wise pastors have always built fences well back from the cliff's edge. Do not counsel a member of the opposite sex alone, behind a closed and windowed-over door, hour after private hour; meet where there is visibility, involve your wife or another mature woman, keep the door and the schedule open to scrutiny. These are not signs of a dirty mind; they are the ordinary prudence of a man who knows his own heart is deceitful and that the strongest have fallen. Transparency is the great protector. The sin that thrives in secrecy withers in the light. A pastor who lives an open life — whose comings and goings, finances, and friendships are visible to those who may rightly ask — has built around himself the very conditions in which integrity is easiest to keep.

Scripture gives us a sobering picture of what secrecy does. Remember how the conquest began: Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground, worshiped at Gilgal, and marched around Jericho until the walls came down. So far, so good. Then came Ai — a small town, an easy target, or so the scouts said. They sent up only three thousand men, and the men of Ai routed them and killed thirty-six. Joshua was staggered; he tore his clothes and fell on his face before the Lord. And then he learned the reason: the Lord had sheathed His sword because of sin. One man, Achan, had taken for himself what belonged to God and hidden it in the earth under his tent — and no one knew. But hidden sin is never as private as the sinner imagines. Like ripples on a stream, it spreads outward; the whole camp had been defeated by what one man buried in the ground. None of us sins alone. The remedy was not deeper secrecy but light: the thing had to be uncovered, named, and dealt with openly before the nation could stand again. So it is with the pastor. The sin you can confess, expose, and bring under the counsel of others loses its power; the sin you bury under the tent only waits, and spreads, and brings down more than yourself.

None of this is to make the ministry cold or to treat every hurting woman as a temptation. It is to take seriously what Scripture says of the human heart and to honor the power the office places in our hands by refusing to abuse it — even by accident, even by carelessness. The man who guards these boundaries is not being suspicious; he is being faithful.
Section 5.3 — Sheep-Stealing and the Ethics of Church Growth

Now to a sin that wears respectable clothes and is rarely named for what it is: the deliberate poaching of another congregation's members to swell one's own. We must be careful and fair here, because not every transfer of membership is theft. People move; people are providentially relocated; people sometimes have legitimate, conscience-driven reasons to leave one fellowship for another, and a pastor may rightly receive a believer who comes to him after leaving his former church in good order. Receiving the one who genuinely comes is not poaching. The sin lies elsewhere — in the heart that recruits, that targets a neighboring flock and courts its people, that quietly fans dissatisfaction in another man's sheep in order to draw them into one's own fold and call the resulting growth a blessing of God.

What is wrong with it is that it treats the kingdom of God as a competition between brothers and a man's own congregation as the prize. Paul will have none of that spirit. "Let nothing be done through selfish ambition or conceit, but in lowliness of mind let each esteem others better than himself" (Philippians 2:3). And to the church he writes of "endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace" (Ephesians 4:3). The man who builds his ministry by tearing down a brother's has gained members and lost the very unity those members were called to embody. He has also, almost always, exposed the true engine of his ministry, which is not love for Christ's whole church but ambition for his own corner of it.

The test of the heart is simple. Do you rejoice when the faithful church across town flourishes, even when it flourishes more than yours? Or does its growth sour something in you? The kingdom is one. Your calling is to build Christ's church, not your brand within it, and a man who cannot be glad at another shepherd's increase has not yet understood whose sheep these are.
Section 5.4 — Living by a Clear Ministerial Code

Everything in this unit comes to rest in a single practice that has served faithful ministers for generations: living by a clear and settled code of ministerial ethics, ideally one a man has thought through and written down before the pressures arrive. The value of a written code is not that it adds rules to grace — we have labored from Unit 1 to keep that order straight — but that it forces a man to decide in the calm what he will do in the storm. The time to resolve how you will handle a confidence, a counseling boundary, or a neighboring church's member is not in the heat of the moment, when desire and self-interest cloud the judgment, but long before, in the clear light of prayer.

Such a code touches the ordinary integrity of ministerial life. It means telling the truth when you give a reference for a man leaving your staff, neither flattering him into another church's pulpit nor quietly destroying him with hints. It means honoring your predecessor rather than building yourself up by running him down to a congregation glad to hear it, and serving your successor by leaving well rather than meddling from the wings once you have gone. It means keeping your word — that a minister's promise, once given, is as good as a bond — and dealing with the church's resources and your own compensation with a transparency that invites scrutiny rather than avoiding it. We will take up the theology of money and stewardship in full in Unit 9; here it is enough to say that financial integrity is simply one more application of the open and honest life this whole unit commends.

The Scriptures give us a stark picture of what it means to keep an oath that has grown costly. When the Gibeonites came to Joshua, they came in disguise — worn-out sandals, cracked wineskins, dry and crumbling bread — pretending to be travelers from a far country so that Israel would make a treaty God had forbidden with the peoples of the land. At the crucial moment Joshua and the leaders did not stop to ask counsel of the Lord, and they were deceived into swearing a covenant, ratified by an oath in the name of the Lord, the God of Israel. Three days later the trick came to light. And here is the part a minister must take to heart: even though he had been deceived, Joshua held to his word. The trickery of the Gibeonites did not nullify the contract. An oath sworn in the name of the Lord was binding, and to break it would have brought God's wrath on the nation — as it later did, generations on, when Saul disregarded that same treaty and his house suffered for it. Joshua rebuked the Gibeonites for their deceit, and he held them to a humble service, but he did not break faith. So it must be with the man of God. He does not wriggle free of a commitment because keeping it has become inconvenient, or because he can now see he agreed too quickly.

Behind all of it stands the watching world. "Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside" (Colossians 4:5). The unbeliever who will never read your statement of faith reads your conduct closely, and a single act of pastoral dishonesty does more to discredit the gospel in his eyes than a hundred sermons can repair. Let your ethics preach. A man whose life is clean, whose word is trustworthy, and whose dealings are open has built a platform from which the gospel can be heard — and that, in the end, is what all these boundaries are for.
Confidentiality is a stewardship, not a wall. Keep a thousand ordinary secrets faithfully — and know the few grave moments when love for the endangered must break the seal.

mc.stem: 1. The trust people place in a pastor with their secrets is best described as:
mc.why: That trust is one of the most sacred things entrusted to the office: built slowly and shattered instantly.

es_reference.stem: 1. La confianza que las personas ponen en un pastor con sus secretos se describe mejor como:
options: Construida lentamente y hecha añicos al instante
es_reference.why: Esa confianza es una de las cosas más sagradas confiadas al oficio: construida lentamente y hecha añicos al instante.

mc.stem: 2. The unit's crucial correction is that confidentiality is:
options: An absolute that must never be broken
mc.why: Confidentiality is a stewardship that serves the soul and protects the flock; it is not an absolute.

es_reference.stem: 2. La corrección crucial de la unidad es que la confidencialidad es:
options: Un absoluto que nunca debe romperse
es_reference.why: La confidencialidad es una mayordomía que sirve al alma y protege a la grey; no es un absoluto.

mc.stem: 3. The seal of confidence yields when keeping it would:
options: Leave someone in danger of serious harm
mc.why: The governing principle: the seal yields when keeping it would leave someone in danger of serious harm.

es_reference.stem: 3. El sello de la confianza cede cuando guardarlo:
options: Violaría los estatutos de la iglesia
Dejaría a alguien en peligro de daño grave
es_reference.why: El principio rector: el sello cede cuando guardarlo dejaría a alguien en peligro de daño grave.

mc.stem: 4. When abuse of a child or vulnerable person is disclosed, the pastor must:
options: Handle it privately to protect the church
Bring it into the light and involve the authorities
mc.why: Protecting the helpless, and often the law, obliges him to bring it into the light and involve the authorities.

es_reference.stem: 4. Cuando se revela el abuso de un niño o persona vulnerable, el pastor debe:
options: Manejarlo en privado para proteger a la iglesia
Traerlo a la luz e involucrar a las autoridades
es_reference.why: Proteger al indefenso, y a menudo la ley, lo obliga a traerlo a la luz e involucrar a las autoridades.

mc.stem: 5. The unit urges a pastor to settle these matters and know the reporting laws of his land:
options: When an elder asks him to
mc.why: Settle your conscience and know the reporting laws before the crisis comes, not in the moment.

es_reference.stem: 5. La unidad exhorta al pastor a resolver estos asuntos y conocer las leyes de denuncia de su tierra:
options: Solo después de que surja una crisis
Cuando un anciano se lo pida
Antes de que llegue la crisis
es_reference.why: Resuelva su conciencia y conozca las leyes de denuncia antes de que llegue la crisis, no en el momento.

mc.stem: 6. The unit frankly states that a pastor, in fact, holds:
mc.why: The pastor is trusted, respected, and given intimate access to the vulnerable: he holds real power.

es_reference.stem: 6. La unidad declara con franqueza que un pastor, de hecho, tiene:
options: Poder igual al de cada miembro
es_reference.why: El pastor es confiado, respetado, y se le da acceso íntimo a los vulnerables: tiene poder real.

mc.stem: 7. The combination that produces the gravest pastoral failures is:
mc.why: Power and proximity together are the soil in which the gravest pastoral failures grow.

es_reference.stem: 7. La combinación que produce los fracasos pastorales más graves es:
es_reference.why: El poder y la cercanía juntos son el suelo en que crecen los fracasos pastorales más graves.

mc.stem: 8. Regarding a sexual entanglement between a pastor and someone under his care, the unit insists it is:
mc.why: Because of the imbalance of power, it is never a meeting of equals; it is an abuse of the office's trust.

es_reference.stem: 8. Respecto a un enredo sexual entre un pastor y alguien bajo su cuidado, la unidad insiste en que es:
es_reference.why: A causa del desequilibrio de poder, nunca es un encuentro entre iguales; es un abuso de la confianza del oficio.

mc.stem: 9. The greater share of guilt in such a case falls on the pastor because:
options: The greater share of the power was his
mc.why: The greater share of the guilt is his because the greater share of the power was his.

es_reference.stem: 9. La mayor parte de la culpa en tal caso recae sobre el pastor porque:
options: La mayor parte del poder era suya
es_reference.why: La mayor parte de la culpa es suya porque la mayor parte del poder era suya.

mc.stem: 10. The unit names which quality as the great protector against secret sin?
mc.why: Transparency is the great protector; the sin that thrives in secrecy withers in the light.

es_reference.stem: 10. ¿A cuál cualidad nombra la unidad como la gran protectora contra el pecado secreto?
es_reference.why: La transparencia es la gran protectora; el pecado que prospera en el secreto se marchita en la luz.

mc.stem: 11. The unit says not every transfer of membership is theft, because people:
mc.why: People move and are providentially relocated; receiving one who comes in good order is not poaching.

es_reference.stem: 11. La unidad dice que no todo traslado de membresía es robo, porque las personas:
options: Se mudan y son providencialmente reubicadas
es_reference.why: La gente se muda y es providencialmente reubicada; recibir a uno que viene en buen orden no es robo.

mc.stem: 12. The sin of sheep-stealing lies specifically in the heart that:
options: Receives a believer who comes in good order
Recruits and courts another flock's people
mc.why: The sin is in the heart that recruits and courts another flock's people, fanning their dissatisfaction.

es_reference.stem: 12. El pecado del robo de ovejas yace específicamente en el corazón que:
options: Recibe a un creyente que viene en buen orden
Da la bienvenida a las visitas
Recluta y corteja a la gente de otra grey
es_reference.why: El pecado está en el corazón que recluta y corteja a la gente de otra grey, avivando su descontento.

mc.stem: 13. Sheep-stealing is wrong because it treats the kingdom of God as:
mc.why: It treats the kingdom as a competition between brothers and one's own congregation as the prize.

es_reference.stem: 13. El robo de ovejas está mal porque trata el reino de Dios como:
es_reference.why: Trata el reino como una competencia entre hermanos y la propia congregación como el premio.

mc.stem: 14. Philippians 2:3 is cited to forbid doing anything through:
mc.why: Philippians 2:3 forbids selfish ambition or conceit, calling each to esteem others better than himself.

es_reference.stem: 14. Filipenses 2:3 se cita para prohibir hacer cualquier cosa por:
es_reference.why: Filipenses 2:3 prohíbe la contienda o la vanagloria, llamando a cada uno a estimar a otros mejores que sí mismo.

mc.stem: 15. The simple test of the heart on church growth is whether a pastor:
options: Rejoices when a faithful church across town flourishes
mc.why: Do you rejoice when the faithful church across town flourishes, even more than yours? The kingdom is one.

es_reference.stem: 15. La prueba sencilla del corazón sobre el crecimiento de la iglesia es si un pastor:
options: Cuenta a sus miembros a menudo
Se regocija cuando una iglesia fiel del otro lado del pueblo florece
es_reference.why: ¿Se regocija cuando la iglesia fiel del otro lado del pueblo florece, aun más que la suya? El reino es uno.

mc.stem: 16. The value of a written ministerial code is that it forces a man to:
options: Decide in the calm what he will do in the storm
mc.why: A written code forces a man to decide in the calm what he will do in the storm.

es_reference.stem: 16. El valor de un código ministerial escrito es que obliga a un hombre a:
options: Decidir en la calma lo que hará en la tormenta
es_reference.why: Un código escrito obliga a un hombre a decidir en la calma lo que hará en la tormenta.

mc.stem: 17. Living by a code includes giving an honest reference, which means neither flattering a departing man nor:
mc.why: An honest reference neither flatters a man into another pulpit nor quietly destroys him with hints.

es_reference.stem: 17. Vivir conforme a un código incluye dar una referencia honesta, lo cual significa ni adular a un hombre que se va ni:
es_reference.why: Una referencia honesta ni adula a un hombre hacia otro púlpito ni lo destruye en silencio con insinuaciones.

mc.stem: 18. A minister's promise, once given, the unit says, should be:
mc.why: Keeping your word means a minister's promise, once given, is as good as a bond.

es_reference.stem: 18. La promesa de un ministro, una vez dada, dice la unidad, debe ser:
es_reference.why: Mantener su palabra significa que la promesa de un ministro, una vez dada, vale tanto como una fianza.

mc.stem: 19. Colossians 4:5 (walk in wisdom toward those who are outside) is used to stress the importance of:
options: The watching world's view of pastoral conduct
mc.why: The watching world reads a pastor's conduct closely; one dishonest act discredits the gospel.

es_reference.stem: 19. Colosenses 4:5 (andad sabiamente para con los de afuera) se usa para recalcar la importancia de:
options: La visión que el mundo que observa tiene de la conducta pastoral
es_reference.why: El mundo que observa lee de cerca la conducta de un pastor; un solo acto deshonesto desacredita el evangelio.

mc.stem: 20. The ultimate purpose of all these boundaries, the unit concludes, is to:
options: Build a platform from which the gospel can be heard
mc.why: All these boundaries exist to build a platform from which the gospel can be heard.

es_reference.stem: 20. El propósito último de todos estos límites, concluye la unidad, es:
options: Edificar una plataforma desde la cual el evangelio puede ser oído
es_reference.why: Todos estos límites existen para edificar una plataforma desde la cual el evangelio puede ser oído.

sa.prompt: 21. Explain why confidentiality is a stewardship rather than an absolute, and name the principle that governs when it yields.
sa.model: Confidentiality is one of the most sacred trusts of the pastoral office, built slowly and shattered instantly; a pastor whom no one can trust with the truth cannot shepherd anyone's soul. Yet it is a stewardship, not an absolute. It was given to serve the good of the soul and the protection of the flock, never to become a wall behind which evil hides and the vulnerable are sacrificed. The governing principle is that the seal of confidence yields when keeping it would leave someone in danger of serious harm. A pastor must settle this before the crisis, so he is not paralyzed in the moment he most needs clarity.

es_reference.prompt: 21. Explique por qué la confidencialidad es una mayordomía y no un absoluto, y nombre el principio que rige cuándo cede.
es_reference.model: La confidencialidad es una de las confianzas más sagradas del oficio pastoral, construida lentamente y hecha añicos al instante; un pastor en quien nadie puede confiar la verdad no puede pastorear el alma de nadie. Sin embargo es una mayordomía, no un absoluto. Fue dada para servir al bien del alma y a la protección de la grey, nunca para llegar a ser un muro tras el cual el mal se esconde y los vulnerables son sacrificados. El principio rector es que el sello de la confianza cede cuando guardarlo dejaría a alguien en peligro de daño grave. El pastor debe resolver esto antes de la crisis, para no quedar paralizado en el momento en que más necesita claridad.

sa.prompt: 22. What must a pastor do when someone discloses intent to harm self or others, or when a child is being abused? Why is silence not discretion?
sa.model: When a person discloses intent to take his own life or harm another, the pastor's duty to protect life overrides his promise of secrecy; he must act to get that person real and immediate help, not merely pray and say nothing. When a child or vulnerable person is being abused, he must bring it into the light and involve the authorities and protective help God has appointed. To stay silent in such cases is not discretion but complicity; the shepherd who shields a wolf to keep a confidence has betrayed the sheep. He should know the reporting laws of his land and settle his conscience before the crisis comes.

es_reference.prompt: 22. ¿Qué debe hacer un pastor cuando alguien revela intención de dañar a sí mismo o a otros, o cuando un niño está siendo abusado? ¿Por qué el silencio no es discreción?
es_reference.model: Cuando una persona revela intención de quitarse la vida o dañar a otro, el deber del pastor de proteger la vida prevalece sobre su promesa de secreto; debe actuar para conseguirle ayuda real e inmediata, no meramente orar y no decir nada. Cuando un niño o persona vulnerable está siendo abusada, debe traerlo a la luz e involucrar a las autoridades y la ayuda protectora que Dios ha designado. Quedarse callado en tales casos no es discreción sino complicidad; el pastor que escuda a un lobo para guardar una confidencia ha traicionado a las ovejas. Debe conocer las leyes de denuncia de su tierra y resolver su conciencia antes de que llegue la crisis.

sa.prompt: 23. Explain why a sexual relationship between a pastor and someone under his care is never a meeting of equals, and where the greater guilt lies.
sa.model: A pastor holds real power: he is trusted, granted spiritual authority, and given intimate access to people at their most vulnerable. Because of that imbalance of power, a sexual or romantic entanglement between a pastor and someone under his care is never a meeting of equals, and the claim that it was mutual is a lie the guilty tell themselves. It is not an affair but an abuse of the trust of the office. The greater share of the guilt is his because the greater share of the power was his.

es_reference.prompt: 23. Explique por qué una relación sexual entre un pastor y alguien bajo su cuidado nunca es un encuentro entre iguales, y dónde yace la mayor culpa.
es_reference.model: Un pastor tiene poder real: es confiado, dotado de autoridad espiritual, y se le da acceso íntimo a las personas en su mayor vulnerabilidad. A causa de ese desequilibrio de poder, un enredo sexual o romántico entre un pastor y alguien bajo su cuidado nunca es un encuentro entre iguales, y la afirmación de que fue mutuo es una mentira que los culpables se dicen. No es una aventura sino un abuso de la confianza del oficio. La mayor parte de la culpa es suya porque la mayor parte del poder era suyo.

sa.prompt: 24. What practical fences guard a pastor against sexual failure, and why is transparency called the great protector?
sa.model: Wise pastors build fences well back from the cliff's edge: not counseling a member of the opposite sex alone behind a closed door hour after hour, but meeting where there is visibility, involving a wife or another mature woman, and keeping the door and schedule open to scrutiny. These are not signs of a dirty mind but ordinary prudence in a man who knows his own heart is deceitful and that the strongest have fallen. Transparency is the great protector, because the sin that thrives in secrecy withers in the light.

es_reference.prompt: 24. ¿Qué cercas prácticas guardan a un pastor contra el fracaso sexual, y por qué se llama a la transparencia la gran protectora?
es_reference.model: Los pastores sabios edifican cercas bien atrás del borde del precipicio: no aconsejar a solas a un miembro del sexo opuesto tras una puerta cerrada hora tras hora, sino reunirse donde haya visibilidad, involucrar a la esposa o a otra mujer madura, y mantener la puerta y el horario abiertos al escrutinio. Estas no son señales de una mente sucia sino prudencia ordinaria en un hombre que sabe que su propio corazón es engañoso y que los más fuertes han caído. La transparencia es la gran protectora, porque el pecado que prospera en el secreto se marchita en la luz.

sa.prompt: 25. Distinguish a legitimate transfer of membership from the sin of sheep-stealing. Where exactly does the sin lie?
sa.model: Not every transfer of membership is theft. People move, are providentially relocated, and sometimes have legitimate, conscience-driven reasons to leave one fellowship for another; receiving a believer who comes in good order is not poaching. The sin lies in the heart that recruits, that targets a neighboring flock and courts its people, and quietly fans dissatisfaction in another man's sheep in order to draw them away and call the growth a blessing of God. It treats the kingdom as a competition between brothers and one's own congregation as the prize.

es_reference.prompt: 25. Distinga un traslado legítimo de membresía del pecado del robo de ovejas. ¿Dónde yace exactamente el pecado?
es_reference.model: No todo traslado de membresía es robo. La gente se muda, es providencialmente reubicada, y a veces tiene razones legítimas, movidas por la conciencia, para dejar una comunión por otra; recibir a un creyente que viene en buen orden no es robo. El pecado yace en el corazón que recluta, que apunta a una grey vecina y corteja a su gente, y en silencio aviva el descontento en las ovejas de otro hombre para atraerlas y llamar al crecimiento una bendición de Dios. Trata el reino como una competencia entre hermanos y la propia congregación como el premio.

sa.prompt: 26. How do Philippians 2:3 and Ephesians 4:3 speak to the ethics of church growth?
sa.model: Paul will have none of the competitive spirit. Philippians 2:3 forbids doing anything through selfish ambition or conceit, calling each instead in lowliness of mind to esteem others better than himself; and Ephesians 4:3 calls believers to endeavor to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. A man who builds his ministry by tearing down a brother's has gained members but lost the very unity those members were called to embody, exposing the true engine of his ministry as ambition for his own corner rather than love for Christ's whole church.

es_reference.prompt: 26. ¿Cómo hablan Filipenses 2:3 y Efesios 4:3 a la ética del crecimiento de la iglesia?
es_reference.model: Pablo no tendrá nada del espíritu competitivo. Filipenses 2:3 prohíbe hacer cualquier cosa por contienda o vanagloria, llamando a cada uno con humildad a estimar a otros mejores que sí mismo; y Efesios 4:3 llama a los creyentes a ser solícitos en guardar la unidad del Espíritu en el vínculo de la paz. El hombre que edifica su ministerio derribando el de un hermano ha ganado miembros pero perdido la unidad misma que esos miembros fueron llamados a encarnar, exponiendo el verdadero motor de su ministerio como ambición por su propio rincón en vez de amor por toda la iglesia de Cristo.

sa.prompt: 27. What is the simple test of the heart regarding another church's growth, and what does failing it reveal?
sa.model: The test of the heart is simple: do you rejoice when the faithful church across town flourishes, even when it flourishes more than yours, or does its growth sour something in you? The kingdom is one, and the pastor's calling is to build Christ's church, not his own brand within it. A man who cannot be glad at another shepherd's increase has not yet understood whose sheep these really are.

es_reference.prompt: 27. ¿Cuál es la prueba sencilla del corazón respecto al crecimiento de otra iglesia, y qué revela el fallarla?
es_reference.model: La prueba del corazón es sencilla: ¿se regocija usted cuando la iglesia fiel del otro lado del pueblo florece, aun cuando florece más que la suya, o su crecimiento agria algo en usted? El reino es uno, y el llamamiento del pastor es edificar la iglesia de Cristo, no su propia marca dentro de ella. Un hombre que no puede alegrarse del aumento de otro pastor aún no ha entendido de quién son en verdad estas ovejas.

sa.prompt: 28. Why does the unit commend a written ministerial code, and what does the saying decide in the calm what you will do in the storm mean?
sa.model: A written ministerial code is commended not because it adds rules to grace, but because it forces a man to decide in the calm what he will do in the storm. The time to resolve how he will handle a confidence, a counseling boundary, or a neighboring church's member is not in the heat of the moment, when desire and self-interest cloud the judgment, but long before, in the clear light of prayer. Settled convictions, written down before the pressures arrive, keep a man from improvising under temptation.

es_reference.prompt: 28. ¿Por qué encomienda la unidad un código ministerial escrito, y qué significa el dicho «decidir en la calma lo que hará en la tormenta»?
es_reference.model: Un código ministerial escrito se encomienda no porque añada reglas a la gracia, sino porque obliga a un hombre a decidir en la calma lo que hará en la tormenta. El tiempo de resolver cómo manejará una confidencia, un límite de consejería, o el miembro de una iglesia vecina no es en el calor del momento, cuando el deseo y el interés propio nublan el juicio, sino mucho antes, en la luz clara de la oración. Convicciones establecidas, puestas por escrito antes de que lleguen las presiones, guardan a un hombre de improvisar bajo la tentación.

sa.prompt: 29. Give three marks of ministerial integrity the code commends (think references, predecessor, promises).
sa.model: The code touches the ordinary integrity of ministerial life. It means giving an honest reference for a departing man, neither flattering him into another pulpit nor quietly destroying him with hints. It means honoring one's predecessor rather than building oneself up by running him down, and serving one's successor by leaving well. And it means keeping one's word, so that a minister's promise, once given, is as good as a bond, with finances handled in a transparency that invites scrutiny.

es_reference.prompt: 29. Dé tres marcas de integridad ministerial que el código encomienda (piense en referencias, predecesor, promesas).
es_reference.model: El código toca la integridad ordinaria de la vida ministerial. Significa dar una referencia honesta de un hombre que se va, ni adulándolo hacia otro púlpito ni destruyéndolo en silencio con insinuaciones. Significa honrar a su predecesor en vez de engrandecerse rebajándolo, y servir a su sucesor dejando el cargo bien. Y significa mantener su palabra, de modo que la promesa de un ministro, una vez dada, vale tanto como una fianza, con las finanzas manejadas en una transparencia que invita al escrutinio.

sa.prompt: 30. How does Colossians 4:5 ground pastoral ethics, and what is the ultimate purpose of all these boundaries?
sa.model: Behind all of it stands the watching world: "Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside" (Colossians 4:5). The unbeliever who will never read a pastor's statement of faith reads his conduct closely, and a single act of pastoral dishonesty does more to discredit the gospel in his eyes than a hundred sermons can repair. So the ultimate purpose of all these boundaries is that a man whose life is clean, whose word is trustworthy, and whose dealings are open has built a platform from which the gospel can be heard. Let your ethics preach.

es_reference.prompt: 30. ¿Cómo fundamenta Colosenses 4:5 la ética pastoral, y cuál es el propósito último de todos estos límites?
es_reference.model: Detrás de todo esto está el mundo que observa: "Andad sabiamente para con los de afuera" (Colosenses 4:5). El incrédulo que nunca leerá la declaración de fe de un pastor lee de cerca su conducta, y un solo acto de deshonestidad pastoral hace más por desacreditar el evangelio ante sus ojos que cien sermones por repararlo. Así, el propósito último de todos estos límites es que un hombre cuya vida es limpia, cuya palabra es digna de confianza y cuyos tratos son abiertos ha construido una plataforma desde la cual el evangelio puede oírse. Que su ética predique.
